title: Work, bureaucracy and formal register
objectives: I can write a formal email or letter with the right greeting, request formulas and closing.
I can handle a job interview and ordinary office situations politely.
I can name the main Brazilian documents and public offices and say what I need from them.
I can choose between o senhor, você and tu depending on the person and the region, and explain why the verb is in the third person.
I can pass on a request and refuse politely.
I can explain why each accent mark, nasal vowel, digraph and acronym in this unit's words is written and pronounced as it is.

vocabulary.note: The letters stand for Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas, the register of individuals that the number comes from. It is said by naming the letters: cê, pê, efe. It is masculine because the noun behind it, cadastro, is masculine. It is asked for in almost every purchase and registration.

example.pt: Preciso informar o meu CPF para abrir a conta.
example.en: I need to give my CPF to open the account.
example.literal: I-need to-inform the my CPF to open the account.

vocabulary.note: The letters stand for Registro Geral. It is said érre, gê: the name of the letter r is written with rr because a single r between vowels would be the tap, and rr keeps the strong sound. Masculine because registro is masculine. Each state issues its own.

example.pt: Esqueci o RG em casa e não consegui entrar no prédio.
example.en: I forgot my ID at home and could not get into the building.
example.literal: I-forgot the RG in house and not I-managed to-enter in-the building.

vocabulary.note: The letters stand for Carteira Nacional de Habilitação. It is said cê, ene, agá: the letter h is silent inside words, but it still has a name, agá. It is feminine because carteira is feminine, while o CPF is masculine: an acronym takes the gender of the noun it abbreviates.

example.pt: A minha CNH vence no mês que vem.
example.en: My driver's license expires next month.
example.literal: The my CNH wins in-the month that comes.

vocabulary.note: Usually a recent utility bill. Comprovante comes from comprovar, to prove, and ends in e, so its stress is on the second to last syllable (com-pro-VAN-te) with no mark. Residência is re-si-DÊN-ci-a: the ending ia counts as two syllables, so the stress is third to last and a mark is required, and the e before n is closed, so it is the circumflex.

example.pt: Pode ser uma conta de luz como comprovante de residência.
example.en: An electricity bill can serve as proof of address.
example.literal: Can be a bill of light as proof of residence.

vocabulary.note: Carteira is the work record booklet, and the employer's signature in it is the proof of a formal contract with legal rights. Assinada is a participle (assinar, to sign) that agrees with the feminine carteira. The ss between vowels is [s]; a single s there would be [z]. Trabalhar de carteira assinada means to have a formal job.

example.pt: Ele finalmente conseguiu um emprego de carteira assinada.
example.en: He finally got a job with a formal contract.
example.literal: He finally managed a job of signed card.

vocabulary.note: Stressed on the third to last syllable (cur-RÍ-cu-lo), which no ending predicts, so the acute accent is written on the stressed i, which always takes the acute. The rr between vowels is the strong r.

example.pt: Enviei o meu currículo para três empresas.
example.en: I sent my CV to three companies.

vocabulary.note: The o is nasal because n closes the first syllable (con-TRA-to), and the final o is said u. The stress is second to last, as the ending o predicts, so there is no mark.

example.pt: Li o contrato com atenção antes de assinar.
example.en: I read the contract carefully before signing.
example.literal: I-read the contract with attention before of to-sign.

vocabulary.note: The ending io counts as two syllables, so the stress falls on the third to last (sa-LÁ-ri-o) and the open a takes the acute. The related dia útil, literally useful day, means business day.

example.pt: O salário é depositado todo quinto dia útil.
example.en: The salary is deposited on the fifth business day of each month.
example.literal: The salary is deposited every fifth useful day.

vocabulary.note: The ending -ção turns a verb into the noun for its act (declarar, declaração). The ç is [s], the ão is a nasal diphthong, and the stress is on the last syllable (de-cla-ra-ÇÃO), as ão predicts, so the tilde is the only mark. The plural is -ções.

example.pt: Preciso entregar a declaração até o fim de maio.
example.en: I need to hand in the declaration by the end of May.
example.literal: I-need to-deliver the declaration until the end of May.

vocabulary.note: Receita means income or revenue, and also a recipe or a prescription; here it is the state's revenue. Receita starts with the strong r, and the c before e is [s]. The l that ends Federal is said [w].

example.pt: A Receita Federal liberou a consulta ao CPF pela internet.
example.en: The federal tax authority made it possible to check a CPF online.
example.literal: The Revenue Federal released the consultation to-the CPF by-the internet.

vocabulary.note: From o prefeito, the mayor. The ei is a diphthong (pre-FEI-tu-ra) and the stress is second to last, so no mark.

example.pt: A prefeitura fica aberta até as cinco da tarde.
example.en: City hall is open until five in the afternoon.
example.literal: The city-hall stays open until the five of-the afternoon.

vocabulary.note: Where signatures are notarized, copies certified and certificates issued. The ending io counts as two syllables, so the stress is third to last (car-TÓ-ri-o) and the open o takes the acute.

example.pt: Fui ao cartório reconhecer firma neste documento.
example.en: I went to the notary office to have my signature notarized on this document.
example.literal: I-went to-the notary-office to-recognize signature in-this document.

vocabulary.note: Said by naming the letters: i, ene, esse, esse. The letters stand for Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social. Masculine because instituto is masculine. It handles pensions and sick pay.

example.pt: Meu avô marcou uma consulta no INSS para pedir a aposentadoria.
example.en: My grandfather scheduled an appointment at the INSS to apply for his pension.
example.literal: My grandfather marked an appointment in-the INSS to ask-for the retirement.

vocabulary.note: Corrente is the adjective for running, current. The rr is the strong r, and the vowels before n are nasal. The adjective comes after the noun, as usual.

example.pt: Gostaria de abrir uma conta corrente neste banco.
example.en: I would like to open a checking account at this bank.
example.literal: I-would-like of to-open an account current in-this bank.

vocabulary.note: Via is a way or a route, and a document's via is one issue of it: the first via is the original, the segunda via the replacement. In segunda the u is a real vowel because it is not followed by e or i, so the g before it is hard: se-GUN-da.

example.pt: Perdi o documento e preciso pedir a segunda via.
example.en: I lost the document and need to ask for a replacement copy.
example.literal: I-lost the document and I-need to-ask-for the second way.

vocabulary.note: The hours during which an office is open, and also its paperwork. The x before a consonant is [s] (ex-pe-di-EN-te), in Rio de Janeiro often [ʃ]. The d before i is said [dʒ]. The stress is second to last, so no mark.

example.pt: O expediente termina às cinco horas.
example.en: Business hours end at five o'clock.
example.literal: The office-hours ends at-the five hours.

vocabulary.note: From atender, to attend to a customer; it is not attendance at an event. The nasal vowels are in the syllables ten and men, and the d before i is said [dʒ].

example.pt: O atendimento neste banco é muito rápido.
example.en: The service at this bank is very fast.

vocabulary.note: Firma here means a signature as a legal mark, not a company (a false friend of firm). The clerk recognizes, that is formally confirms, that the signature is yours. Nh is one sound, [ɲ], and c before e is [s]: re-co-nhe-CER.

example.pt: Para vender o carro, preciso reconhecer firma no cartório.
example.en: To sell the car, I have to have my signature notarized at the notary office.
example.literal: To sell the car, I-need recognize signature in-the notary-office.

vocabulary.note: To stamp a copy as a true copy of the original. The au is a diphthong, and the c before a is [k]. It ends in r, so the stress is on the last syllable: au-ten-ti-CAR.

example.pt: Preciso autenticar estas cópias antes de entregar.
example.en: I need to certify these copies before handing them in.
example.literal: I-need to-authenticate these copies before of to-deliver.

vocabulary.note: From a agenda, the diary or calendar; it is a false friend of English agenda, a list of topics. G before e is [ʒ]. Marcar means the same and is more common in speech.

example.pt: Posso agendar um horário pelo telefone?
example.en: Can I book a time by phone?
example.literal: Can-I schedule a time by-the phone?

vocabulary.note: Also a password or PIN. The nh is a single sound, [ɲ], like the ny of canyon.

example.pt: Peguei uma senha e esperei a minha vez.
example.en: I took a queue number and waited for my turn.
example.literal: I-grabbed a ticket and I-waited the my turn.

vocabulary.note: Used as a respectful word for you to a man, with the third person verb. Ends in r, so the stress is on the last syllable (se-NHOR); the nh is one sound. Feminine a senhora, plural os senhores and as senhoras. Without the article it is a form of address: Bom dia, senhor.

example.pt: O senhor trabalha aqui há muito tempo?
example.en: Have you worked here for a long time, sir?
example.literal: The sir works here there-is much time?

vocabulary.note: The respectful word for you to a woman, with the third person verb. Ends in a, so the stress is second to last (se-NHO-ra), with no mark.

example.pt: A senhora quer sentar?
example.en: Would you like to sit, ma'am?
example.literal: The lady wants to-sit?

vocabulary.note: The participle of prezar, to esteem, used as an adjective, so it agrees with the person: prezado, prezada, prezados, prezadas. The z between vowels is [z]. Used in the opening of a formal letter: Prezado senhor, Prezada doutora.

example.pt: Prezado senhor, escrevo para solicitar informações.
example.en: Dear sir, I am writing to request information.
example.literal: Esteemed sir, I-write to request informations.

vocabulary.note: A standard closing. The adverb is built from the feminine adjective atenciosa plus the suffix -mente, which comes from a Latin word for mind, so the word says with an attentive mind. A -mente adverb keeps the stress of the adjective and adds its own on men: a-ten-ci-o-sa-MEN-te. Cordialmente is slightly warmer.

example.pt: Atenciosamente, Paulo Andrade.
example.en: Sincerely, Paulo Andrade.
example.literal: Attentively, Paulo Andrade.

dialogues.title: At the notary office
dialogues.context: Seu Henrique needs a signature notarized and copies certified. The clerk, Sônia, helps him with the formal process and addresses him as o senhor.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Bom dia, senhor. O senhor pegou uma senha?
lines.en: Good morning, sir. Did you take a queue number?
lines.literal: Good day, sir. The sir picked-up a ticket?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Bom dia. Peguei, sim, a de número quarenta e dois.
lines.en: Good morning. Yes, I did, the one with number forty-two.
lines.literal: Good day. I-picked-up, yes, the one of number forty and two.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Pois não, em que posso ajudar o senhor?
lines.en: Of course, how can I help you, sir?
lines.literal: Well no, in what can-I help the sir?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Gostaria de reconhecer firma neste contrato e de autenticar duas cópias do meu RG.
lines.en: I would like to have my signature notarized on this contract and to certify two copies of my ID.
lines.literal: I-would-like of to-recognize signature in-this contract and of to-authenticate two copies of-the my RG.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Perfeito. O senhor trouxe o documento original e o CPF?
lines.en: Perfect. Did you bring the original document and your CPF?
lines.literal: Perfect. The sir brought the document original and the CPF?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Trouxe o RG e a CNH. O CPF eu não trouxe, mas o número está na CNH.
lines.en: I brought my ID and my license. I didn't bring my CPF, but the number is on the license.
lines.literal: I-brought the RG and the CNH. The CPF I not brought, but the number is in-the CNH.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Sem problema. Preciso só que o senhor assine aqui na minha frente.
lines.en: No problem. I just need you to sign here in front of me.
lines.literal: Without problem. I-need only that the sir sign here in-the my front.

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Claro. Pronto. Quanto fica o total?
lines.en: Of course. Done. How much is the total?
lines.literal: Clear. Ready. How-much stays the total?

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Fica em quarenta reais. O senhor prefere pagar em dinheiro ou no cartão?
lines.en: It comes to forty reais. Do you prefer to pay in cash or by card?
lines.literal: Stays in forty reais. The sir prefers to-pay in money or in-the card?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: No cartão, por favor. Até que horas vai o expediente?
lines.en: By card, please. Until what time are you open?
lines.literal: In-the card, please. Until what hours goes the office-hours?

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Até as dezessete horas, caso o senhor precise voltar. Aqui está o recibo.
lines.en: Until five p.m., in case you need to come back. Here is the receipt.
lines.literal: Until the seventeen hours, in-case the sir need to-return. Here is the receipt.

dialogues.title: A job interview
dialogues.context: Gabriel is interviewing for a position at an office. The interviewer, Patrícia, is a manager. She calls him você, while he addresses her as a senhora and doutora.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Bom dia, Gabriel. Fique à vontade. Obrigada por ter vindo.
lines.en: Good morning, Gabriel. Make yourself comfortable. Thank you for coming.
lines.literal: Good day, Gabriel. Stay at-the will. Obliged for to-have come.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Bom dia, doutora. Obrigado pela oportunidade.
lines.en: Good morning, doctor. Thank you for the opportunity.
lines.literal: Good day, doctor. Obliged by-the opportunity.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Li o seu currículo. Você pode me falar um pouco sobre a sua experiência?
lines.en: I read your CV. Can you tell me a little about your experience?
lines.literal: I-read the your CV. You can to-me speak a little about the your experience?

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Claro. Trabalhei quatro anos numa loja de eletrônicos, no atendimento ao cliente. Depois fui promovido a supervisor.
lines.en: Of course. I worked for four years at an electronics store, in customer service. Then I was promoted to supervisor.
lines.literal: Clear. I-worked four years in-a store of electronics, in-the service to-the client. Afterwards I-was promoted to supervisor.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: E por que você saiu de lá?
lines.en: And why did you leave?
lines.literal: And for what you left of there?

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Eu queria uma oportunidade com mais chance de crescimento. A senhora poderia me explicar como funciona o plano de carreira aqui?
lines.en: I wanted an opportunity with more room for growth. Could you explain to me how the career plan works here?
lines.literal: I wanted an opportunity with more chance of growth. The lady could me explain how works the plan of career here?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Claro. Depois de seis meses, há uma avaliação de desempenho, e as promoções são discutidas uma vez por ano.
lines.en: Of course. After six months there is a performance review, and promotions are discussed once a year.
lines.literal: Clear. After of six months, there-is an evaluation of performance, and the promotions are discussed one time per year.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: A vaga é de carteira assinada? E qual é o horário de trabalho?
lines.en: Is the position a formal job? And what are the working hours?
lines.literal: The vacancy is of signed card? And which is the schedule of work?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: É de carteira assinada, das nove às dezoito horas, de segunda a sexta. O salário e os benefícios serão detalhados na proposta.
lines.en: It is a formal job, from nine to six, Monday to Friday. The salary and benefits will be detailed in the offer.
lines.literal: Is of signed card, of-the nine to-the eighteen hours, of Monday to Friday. The salary and the benefits will-be detailed in-the proposal.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Perfeito. Quando a senhora pretende dar uma resposta?
lines.en: Perfect. When do you plan to give an answer?
lines.literal: Perfect. When the lady intends to-give an answer?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Entraremos em contato por e-mail até sexta-feira. Infelizmente, hoje não posso adiantar mais nada.
lines.en: We will contact you by email by Friday. Unfortunately, I can't say anything more today.
lines.literal: We-will-enter in contact by email until Friday. Unfortunately, today not I-can advance more nothing.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Combinado. Muito obrigado, doutora, e uma ótima tarde.
lines.en: Agreed. Thank you very much, doctor, and have a great afternoon.
lines.literal: Combined. Much obliged, doctor, and a great afternoon.

dialogues.title: Opening an account at the bank
dialogues.context: Dona Marta goes with her daughter Letícia to the bank to open a checking account. The manager, Rodrigo, explains what is missing.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Boa tarde, dona Marta. Em que posso ajudar a senhora?
lines.en: Good afternoon, Dona Marta. How can I help you?
lines.literal: Good afternoon, lady Marta. In what can-I help the lady?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Boa tarde, Rodrigo. Minha filha quer abrir uma conta corrente, e eu vim acompanhar.
lines.en: Good afternoon, Rodrigo. My daughter wants to open a checking account, and I came along.
lines.literal: Good afternoon, Rodrigo. My daughter wants to-open an account current, and I came to-accompany.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Boa tarde. Eu trouxe o RG, o CPF e o comprovante de residência.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I brought my ID, my CPF and my proof of address.
lines.literal: Good afternoon. I brought the RG, the CPF and the proof of residence.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Ótimo, deixa eu conferir. O comprovante precisa estar no seu nome e ser dos últimos três meses.
lines.en: Great, let me check. The proof of address must be in your name and be from the last three months.
lines.literal: Great, lets I check. The proof needs to-be in-the your name and to-be of-the last three months.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Ele está no nome da minha mãe, porque eu moro com ela.
lines.en: It is in my mother's name, because I live with her.
lines.literal: He is in-the name of-the my mother, because I live with her.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Entendi. Infelizmente não posso aceitar assim, mas tem uma solução. A dona Marta pode assinar uma declaração dizendo que a Letícia mora com ela.
lines.en: I see. Unfortunately I can't accept it like that, but there is a solution. Dona Marta can sign a statement saying that Letícia lives with her.
lines.literal: I-understood. Unfortunately not I-can accept thus, but has a solution. The lady Marta can sign a declaration saying that the Letícia lives with her.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Posso assinar agora mesmo. Preciso reconhecer firma no cartório?
lines.en: I can sign right now. Do I need to have my signature notarized at the notary office?
lines.literal: I-can sign now same. I-need recognize signature in-the notary-office?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Não precisa, a senhora assina aqui na minha frente. Depois disso eu agendo a entrega do cartão.
lines.en: No need, you sign here in front of me. After that I will schedule the delivery of the card.
lines.literal: Not needs, the lady signs here in-the my front. After of-that I schedule the delivery of-the card.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Que alívio! E tem alguma tarifa mensal?
lines.en: What a relief! And is there a monthly fee?
lines.literal: What relief! And has some fee monthly?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Para esta conta, não tem. O cartão chega na sua casa em até sete dias úteis.
lines.en: For this account, there isn't one. The card arrives at your home within seven business days.
lines.literal: For this account, not has. The card arrives in-the your house in until seven useful days.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Muito obrigada, meu filho. Foi um ótimo atendimento.
lines.en: Thank you very much, dear. It was excellent service.
lines.literal: Much obliged, my son. Was a great service.

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: accents and stress in the words of this unit
grammar.explanation:
Every accent mark in this unit's words comes out of one procedure from the stress lesson: divide the word into syllables, find the stressed syllable by ear, compare it with the default for the word's ending, and write a mark only when the two disagree. The default is this. Words ending in a, e or o (with or without a final s), or in am, em or ens, are stressed on the second to last syllable. Words ending in anything else, including i, u, l, r, z and the nasal endings ã and ão, are stressed on the last syllable. A word that obeys its default carries no mark. Which mark is then written is decided by the vowel: the acute (´) for an open vowel, and for i and u, which have only one quality; the circumflex (^) for a closed e, o or a. The tilde (~) does a different job, which is to make a vowel nasal. Nothing here has to be memorized word by word; each mark can be recomputed.

Group 1, no mark, because the default already predicts the stress. Senhor (se-NHOR), autenticar (au-ten-ti-CAR), agendar (a-gen-DAR) and reconhecer (re-co-nhe-CER) end in r, so the stress is last. Senha (SE-nha), contrato (con-TRA-to), prezado (pre-ZA-do), tarifa (ta-RI-fa), Henrique (hen-RI-que), expediente (ex-pe-di-EN-te) and atendimento (a-ten-di-MEN-to) end in a, o or e, so the stress is second to last. Declaração (de-cla-ra-ÇÃO), avaliação and promoção end in ão, which defaults to the last syllable, and the tilde already shows the nasal vowel, so nothing more is written.

Group 2, stress on the third to last syllable. No ending predicts this, so a mark is always written: currículo (cur-RÍ-cu-lo), número (NÚ-me-ro), cópias (CÓ-pi-as), ótimo and ótima (Ó-ti-mo), últimos (ÚL-ti-mos), rápido (RÁ-pi-do), eletrônicos (e-le-TRÔ-ni-cos). The vowel chooses the mark. Currículo, número, cópias, ótimo, últimos and rápido take the acute: the stressed vowel is an open a or o, or it is an i or u, which have only one quality. In eletrônicos the stressed o is followed by n, which nasalizes it and closes it, so the circumflex.

Group 3, words ending in a vowel plus a weak i or u (ia, io and similar). For the stress rule Portuguese counts the i as a syllable of its own, so these words are stressed on the third to last syllable and need a mark, even though they look like words ending in a or o. Salário (sa-LÁ-ri-o), cartório (car-TÓ-ri-o), horário (ho-RÁ-ri-o), benefícios (be-ne-FÍ-ci-os), alívio (a-LÍ-vi-o), Patrícia (pa-TRÍ-ci-a) and Letícia (le-TÍ-ci-a) take the acute. Residência (re-si-DÊN-ci-a), agência (a-GÊN-ci-a), experiência (ex-pe-ri-ÊN-ci-a) and Sônia (SÔ-ni-a) take the circumflex, because the stressed vowel is followed by n, which nasalizes and closes it.

Group 4, stress on the last syllable although the ending predicts the second to last. Você (vo-CÊ), até (a-TÉ), também (tam-BÉM), está (es-TÁ), lá and já are all stressed last, so they carry a mark. A one-syllable word that is stressed and ends in a, e or o (with or without s) is written with a mark too, as the small unstressed words are not: é, só, já, há, três, mês. That is the whole difference between é (is) and e (and), and between está (is) and esta (this).

Group 5, the opposite: an ending that predicts the last syllable, but the stress is earlier. Words ending in l, and in i or is, are stressed last by default, so possível (pos-SÍ-vel), útil (Ú-til) and úteis (Ú-teis) need the acute to show that the stress is on the earlier syllable.

Two marks are not about stress. The grave accent of à and às is the crase, the preposition a fused with the article a (a + a = à, a + as = às): à vontade, às cinco horas. And há (there is, or ago) carries its accent to separate it from the preposition a.

Worked example, comprovante de residência. Comprovante is com-pro-VAN-te; it ends in e, so the stress is second to last and no mark is needed. Residência: the ending ia counts as two syllables, so the stress is third to last, which no ending predicts, so a mark is required; the stressed e is followed by n, so it is closed, and the mark is the circumflex.

examples.pt: O horário de atendimento é das nove às dezoito horas.
examples.en: The service hours are from nine to six.
examples.literal: The schedule of service is of-the nine to-the eighteen hours.

examples.pt: Mande o currículo e um comprovante de residência.
examples.en: Send your CV and a proof of address.
examples.literal: Send the CV and a proof of residence.

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: letters and letter groups in the words of this unit
grammar.explanation:
Portuguese spelling is a code in which something you can see decides the sound: the letter that comes next, the position in the word, or a mark. The words of this unit are mostly official vocabulary built from Latin, which is where the code is most regular. This note reads them with the rules of the first lesson, and the table at the end lists each pattern once.

Acronyms first. CPF, RG, CNH and INSS (and FGTS in the culture note) are said by naming the letters, which you met in the alphabet lesson: CPF is cê-pê-efe, RG is érre-gê, CNH is cê-ene-agá, INSS is i-ene-esse-esse. The letter h has a name, agá, even though it is silent inside words. Each acronym takes the gender of the noun it abbreviates, which is why the article differs: o CPF (cadastro, masculine), o RG (registro, masculine), o INSS (instituto, masculine), but a CNH (carteira, feminine).

The sound [s] has several spellings, and the next letter chooses between them. C is [s] before e or i (residência, agência, Receita, Letícia, atenciosamente) and [k] before a, o, u or another consonant (cartório, currículo, contrato, autenticar, esclarecimento). To write [s] before a, o or u the cedilla is used: ç. The ending -ção (plural -ções) is the usual way to turn a verb into the noun for its act or result: declarar, declaração; informar, informação; promover, promoção; avaliar, avaliação. It is said with the nasal diphthong of pão and is stressed on its last syllable. Between two vowels a single s would be [z], so [s] is written ss: assinar, assinada, assim, dezessete. Compare prezado and dezoito, where the z between vowels is [z]. An s or x that ends a syllable before a voiceless consonant (p, t, c, f, q) is [s] in most of Brazil and [ʃ] in the city of Rio de Janeiro: expediente, experiência, esclarecimento, sexta. Before a voiced consonant (b, d, g, m, n and similar) an s is [z], or [ʒ] in Rio de Janeiro: mesmo, desde.

G works the same way. Before e or i it is [ʒ], the s of 'measure' (agência, agendar, gerência); before a, o or u it is [g] (segunda, Rodrigo). To get the hard sound before e or i, gu is written and the u is silent: peguei, conseguiu, segue. Before a the u of gu and qu is pronounced like a w: aguardo, quarenta, quatro, qualquer. Before e or i, qu is [k] with a silent u: que, Henrique. A few words such as frequente and cinquenta pronounce the u anyway and are learned word by word. J is always [ʒ]: ajudar.

The digraphs, pairs of letters that spell one sound. Nh is [ɲ], like the ny of 'canyon' (senha, senhor, senhora, reconhecer, desempenho). Lh is [ʎ], like the lli of 'million' (trabalho, trabalhei, filha, detalhados). Ch is [ʃ], the sh of 'shoe' (chance, a French loan word that keeps its spelling). H alone is silent: Henrique, horário, hoje.

The letter r is strong [h] at the start of a word and after n, l or s, and when doubled between vowels (Receita, Henrique, currículo, corrente). It is a tap between vowels or after a consonant in the same syllable (carteira, prazo, contrato, entrevista, prefeitura). At the end of a syllable (cartório, firma, senhor) it varies by region.

Sounds that depend on position. An l that ends a syllable is said [w]: Federal, original, mensal. In most of Brazil, t and d become [tʃ] and [dʒ] before an i and before a weak final e, which is said like i: atendimento, pretende, oportunidade, tarde, atenciosamente. A vowel followed by m or n in the same syllable is nasal and the m or n is not said as a consonant: contrato, comprovante, entrevista, informar, mensal. The word ending em is the nasal diphthong of também and em. Ou is said [o] in everyday speech (doutora, trouxe), and ei is [ej] (Receita, prefeitura). The letter x between vowels has no rule and is learned word by word: anexo has [ks], trouxe and próxima have [s].

Finally, hyphens. Sexta-feira is a compound noun, sente-se attaches the pronoun se to the verb, and e-mail is an English loan word written with its hyphen and read with Portuguese sounds.

grammar.title: Formal address: o senhor, a senhora and titles
grammar.explanation:
Portuguese builds respect into the grammar. English has one word for you and shows respect with tone and extra words: sir, please, could you. Portuguese has several words for you, and the choice tells the listener how you see them. The three ordinary choices in Brazil are você (neutral, everyday), o senhor and a senhora (respectful), and tu (regional, covered in a later note of this unit). The verb must match the choice, and there is a reason for it.

The reason is that o senhor and a senhora are noun phrases. Senhor means lord, master, gentleman. When you say O senhor quer um café? you are literally asking 'Does the gentleman want a coffee?', speaking about the person you are speaking to. Any noun phrase takes a third person verb, so o senhor quer, a senhora trouxe and você pode all have the third person singular ending. Você itself began as a title, Vossa Mercê ('Your Mercy'), worn down over centuries to vosmecê and then você. The plurals are os senhores, as senhoras and vocês.

The same logic decides the possessive. Seu and sua are the third person possessives, so they also mean your for você, o senhor and a senhora: o seu nome, your name. Where that could be unclear, Brazilians use the senhor's own noun phrase: o nome do senhor, 'the name of the gentleman'.

Articles. As a subject or an object, o senhor keeps its article: O senhor pegou uma senha? Em que posso ajudar o senhor? When you call the person directly, as English does with 'Good morning, sir', the article is dropped: Bom dia, senhor. The same holds for senhora.

Titles before names. Brazilians address people by a title plus the first name far more often than by the surname. Seu is a reduced form of senhor used before a man's first name (seu Henrique, seu José); it is respectful and warm, often used for older men. It is not the possessive seu, although it is spelled identically. Dona, from the Latin for lady, does the same for a woman (dona Marta). Doutor and doutora are used for doctors, lawyers and other professionals, not only for people with doctorates: in the interview Gabriel calls the manager doutora. In familiar speech a name can take an article: a dona Marta, a Letícia.

Whom to call o senhor. Older people, strangers in a service setting, clients, and superiors, especially in public offices. The relationship need not be symmetrical: Patrícia says você to Gabriel, and he answers with a senhora. When in doubt be formal; people will say Pode me chamar de você when they want you to relax.

grammar.title: Formal letters and emails: the fixed frame
grammar.explanation:
Formal writing is a fixed frame so that the reader can process the message quickly: an opening, a statement of purpose, the body, a closing, and a name. Nothing in the frame is improvised; you recognize it and reuse it.

The opening is Prezado senhor, Prezada senhora, Prezados senhores or Prezado Paulo Andrade, followed by a comma. Prezado is the participle of prezar, to esteem, used as an adjective, so the literal meaning is 'esteemed sir'. As an adjective it agrees in gender and number with the person addressed: prezado, prezada, prezados, prezadas. English does the same job with dear. A title can follow: Prezada doutora Patrícia. If you know the person well, Olá, João is acceptable, but with a stranger, start formal.

The closing is Atenciosamente ('attentively') or Cordialmente ('cordially'), then your name. Both are adverbs made by one recipe: take the feminine form of the adjective (atenciosa; cordial has only one form) and add the suffix -mente. The suffix comes from a Latin word for mind, so atenciosamente is in origin 'with an attentive mind'. Cordialmente is a little warmer; Att. is the common abbreviation in short messages; in informal workplace emails Abraço or Obrigado is typical.

The tone of the body stays formal: third person forms for the person you address (o senhor, a senhora), the fixed request formulas of the next note, and a clear purpose in the first sentence. Reply emails from companies often use the first person plural: agradecemos o seu interesse, 'we thank you for your interest'.

grammar.title: Request formulas for polite requests
grammar.explanation:
Politeness in Portuguese, as in English, works mostly by indirectness: the more direct a sentence, the ruder it sounds, so polite speech adds distance. There are three ordinary tools. The first is a question in place of a command: Poderia me informar...? asks whether you are able, where Informe-me is an order. The second is a tense that moves the sentence away from the present and from certainty. Gostaria and poderia are the conditional (the form for what would happen), the same effect as English would like and could; eu queria, the imperfect, softens in the way English I was wondering does. The third is a fixed formula that both sides recognize as formal, which is the main business of written Portuguese.

The forms. Gostaria de plus an infinitive (Gostaria de solicitar, Gostaria de saber) states a wish; gostar always takes de before what you like, so the de stays even when an infinitive follows. Poderia plus an infinitive asks for help. In a request to an adult you do not know, add o senhor or a senhora: O senhor poderia...? The object pronoun me goes before the infinitive in Brazilian speech and writing: Poderia me informar. The traditional Poderia informar-me, with the pronoun after the verb and a hyphen, is correct but now sounds stiff.

Written formulas. Venho por meio desta is literally 'I come by means of this'. Desta is de + esta, and esta points to an omitted feminine noun such as carta or mensagem, so the full thought is 'I come by means of this letter', which means 'I am writing to'. Solicito is the first person present of solicitar, to request formally. Segue em anexo is literally 'follows in attachment': the attached thing is the subject of segue, and anexo is a noun meaning attachment, so it does not agree; with a plural thing, careful writing says Seguem em anexo os documentos. Fico à disposição is 'I remain at your disposition' (ficar, to remain; à is the crase of a + a). Aguardo retorno is 'I await reply': aguardar takes its object directly, with no preposition. Agradeço desde já is 'I thank since already', that is, thanks in advance. Conforme conversamos is 'as we talked'. All of these use the first person present, because the writer performs the act by writing it.

Spoken softeners complete the picture: por favor; com licença, literally 'with license', i.e. with permission, used before interrupting or passing; and por gentileza, literally 'by kindness', a little more formal than por favor. A request without any of these can sound abrupt in a public office, even when the grammar is correct.

grammar.title: Tu, você and o senhor: choosing address forms
grammar.explanation:
Brazilian Portuguese has three ordinary ways of saying you to one person, and they differ in two things: how much respect they carry, and which verb form they take. Você is the standard, unmarked form across most of Brazil and takes the third person singular verb (você fala). O senhor and a senhora are the respectful forms, also with the third person. Tu is the old second person pronoun; it survives in parts of the country, either with its own verb form (tu falas) or, very often, with the third person verb (tu fala).

Why two tu patterns exist. In the older system tu had endings of its own, ending in -s: tu falas, tu queres, tu falaste. As você spread as the everyday form, the regions that kept tu kept the pronoun; in many of them the special endings wore away, giving tu fala and tu quer. Where the full endings survive, as in parts of the North and some areas of the far south, tu falas is heard. Tu is used in the far south, in parts of the North and Northeast, and in some neighborhoods of Rio de Janeiro. In some of those places você is actually the more distant form, so the choice there is not simply informal versus formal.

Both tu patterns are common in speech, but school grammar and formal writing expect você, o senhor or the correct tu endings. As a learner, you can use você everywhere and understand tu when you hear it. Never use tu in a formal setting. The plural does not vary: vocês works everywhere, and vós survives only in prayers and old texts.

The imperative shows the same split. The neutral and formal commands are built from the você form of the present subjunctive: sente-se, aguarde, entre. Casual speech in tu regions uses the tu command, which is the same as the third person present indicative: senta, espera, entra. To a stranger in an office always use the formal command or, better, a polite question: O senhor poderia aguardar?

grammar.title: Reported requests and polite refusals
grammar.explanation:
Passing on a request means reporting an act of asking, and that involves three people: the one who asks, the one who is asked, and the one who must act. The verb pedir, to ask for, builds this in two ways. Careful speech and writing use pedir que plus a subjunctive verb. The subjunctive is the mood for things that are wanted but have not happened, and a request is exactly that. Its tense follows the main verb: a present main verb takes the present subjunctive (Pedimos que traga o RG, 'we ask that you bring your ID'; traga is trazer in the present subjunctive) and a past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive (Ela pediu que eu enviasse o contrato). Everyday speech prefers pedir para plus the infinitive: Ela pediu para eu enviar o contrato. The person who acts comes right after para, and because the subject of an infinitive is a subject, it is eu and not mim: para eu enviar is correct, and para mim enviar is a common error, since mim is only for objects of prepositions. When the person asked is the one who acts, you can also make that person the object: Ela me pediu para enviar o contrato. English says 'asked me to send' with no change of mood.

Mandar is the stronger verb: O chefe mandou entregar hoje is 'the boss ordered it handed in today', an order rather than a request.

To report what someone said, use dizer or falar plus que: Ele disse que ia ligar. The ia is the imperfect of ir, so the sentence says 'he said that he was going to call'. The imperfect appears because the plan was in the past when he spoke, in the same way that English turns 'is going to' into 'was going to'. A later unit treats the reporting of speech in full.

Polite refusals. In formal Portuguese a bare não is abrupt. The principle is again distance. Use the future or conditional in place of the present (será, poderei in place of é, posso); add a softener (infelizmente, lamento, receio); state the situation instead of the refusal (no momento não temos vagas, 'at the moment we have no openings'); and offer something (podemos agendar para segunda). Receio que não seja possível uses the subjunctive after receio, I fear, because a feeling about something uncertain triggers it. Lamento informar que... is the standard opening for bad news. In friendly talk Não dá, desculpa is perfectly fine: dar here means to work out, so não dá is 'it does not work out'. At a counter or in a letter the longer formula is expected.

grammar.title: Phrases in the dialogues: literal meaning and use
grammar.explanation:
Several phrases in the dialogues do not mean what their words say. This note separates three things for each: the literal words, the natural English, and when the phrase is used. A phrase is a fixed unit; once you know the literal words, you can see why the idiom was formed, and you remember it better than a translation alone.

Pois não is literally 'well no'. A clerk or waiter says it to mean 'of course, how can I help you?'. The underlying logic is a polite answer to an implied question: is there any problem in my serving you? Well, no. It is a service formula, not a refusal. Fique à vontade is 'stay at the will', that is, stay as you wish, make yourself comfortable. Fique is the command of ficar, to stay, and the c changes to qu before the e, as in the command lesson.

Ficar also appears in prices. Quanto fica o total? is 'how much does the total stay?', and Fica em quarenta reais is 'it stays at forty reais': fica is how a sum settles, so it means it comes to. Deixa eu conferir is 'let me check'; deixa is the informal command of deixar, to let (the same form as the third person present), and colloquial Portuguese keeps the subject pronoun eu after it where the textbook writes deixe-me conferir. Pronto, literally 'ready', means done or all set. Agora mesmo is 'now same', right now. Combinado, 'combined', is 'agreed'. Que alívio! is 'what relief'. Meu filho, literally 'my son', is an affectionate address from an older person to a younger one.

A false friend, a conjunction and two short past forms. Pretender does not mean to pretend but to intend, to plan: Quando a senhora pretende dar uma resposta? is 'when do you intend to give an answer?'. Caso means in case and is followed by the subjunctive: caso o senhor precise voltar. Two past forms are short because their stems are short. Li, I read, is ler in the preterite: the stem l- plus the ending -i. Saiu, you left, is sair: the stem sa- plus the ending -iu.

Word order. O CPF eu não trouxe puts the object first for emphasis: 'the CPF, I did not bring'. Portuguese allows this freely, because the pronoun eu and the verb ending still show who does what. And Portuguese has no it: ele in Ele está no nome da minha mãe refers to the masculine comprovante, so it can be translated it, but the pronoun is he because the noun is masculine.

culture.title: A burocracia brasileira
culture.text:
Brazilian bureaucracy has a reputation for papers, stamps and queues, and a few words tell the story. The cartório is an office, run privately under public authority, where you register births and marriages, notarize signatures (reconhecer firma) and certify copies (autenticar). The CPF number is asked for at pharmacies, shops and websites, and cashiers often ask Quer CPF na nota? Many people hire a despachante, a professional who handles paperwork for them, especially for cars and property. Acronyms that cannot be read as a word, such as CPF, RG, CNH, INSS and FGTS, are said by naming the letters.

Working life has its own vocabulary. A job with carteira assinada means formal employment with legal protections: paid vacation, a thirteenth-month salary (décimo terceiro) paid in December, and a contribution to a savings fund called FGTS. In recent years many services have moved online, through the government portal gov.br, and the work booklet is now digital, but physical queues, with a numbered ticket (a senha), remain common at the INSS, the bank and city hall.

Income tax is declared to the Receita Federal every year, with a deadline at the end of May that makes the news. In offices, the tone is polite and the title matters: seu José, dona Rita, doutora Ana. The forms seu and dona are used with first names, not surnames, and mix respect with warmth, something English titles such as Mr. and Mrs. with a surname do not. A smile and a por favor go a long way at the counter, and so does patience.

paragraphs.en: Dear Mr. Paulo, thank you for your interest. Unfortunately, it will not be possible to schedule the interview next week, since the management calendar is full.
paragraphs.literal: Esteemed sir Paulo, we-thank the your interest. Unfortunately, not will-be possible to-mark the interview in-the next week, since the agenda of-the management is complete.

paragraphs.pt: As informações sobre salário e benefícios serão passadas durante a entrevista. O senhor poderia comparecer à nossa sede no dia vinte e dois, às catorze horas?
paragraphs.en: Information about salary and benefits will be given during the interview. Could you come to our headquarters on the twenty-second, at two p.m.?
paragraphs.literal: The informations about salary and benefits will-be passed during the interview. The sir could appear at-the our headquarters on-the day twenty and two, at-the fourteen hours?

paragraphs.pt: Pedimos que traga o RG, o CPF e um comprovante de residência. Cordialmente, Fernanda Lima.
paragraphs.en: We ask that you bring your ID, your CPF and a proof of address. Cordially, Fernanda Lima.
paragraphs.literal: We-ask that bring the RG, the CPF and a proof of residence. Cordially, Fernanda Lima.

questions.prompt: Why did Paulo write the email?
choices: To ask for a salary increase
questions.explanation: He uses Venho por meio desta me candidatar à vaga, where desta points to the message he is writing.

questions.prompt: Besides the interview, what information does Paulo ask about?
questions.explanation: He asks to solicitar informações sobre o salário e os benefícios.

questions.prompt: Why can't the interview happen next week?
questions.explanation: The reply says a agenda da gerência está completa.

questions.prompt: What should Paulo bring to the interview?
choices: His ID, CPF and proof of address
questions.explanation: The last paragraph asks for the RG, o CPF e um comprovante de residência.

questions.prompt: In the reply, why is the refusal written não será possível and not não é possível?
choices: The future tense adds distance and softens the refusal
The event is in the past
Será is the only form the verb ser has in writing
The writer is unsure about the facts
questions.explanation: Formal refusals move away from the present: will not be possible sounds gentler than is not possible.

questions.prompt: Why does the reply say Pedimos que traga and not Pedimos que trazer?
choices: Pedir que requires the subjunctive, here the present subjunctive traga
questions.explanation: A request is about something not yet done, so the verb after que is subjunctive; the main verb is in the present, so the subjunctive is in the present.

exercises.prompt: Why does the verb after o senhor use the third person (O senhor quer um café?)?
choices: Because o senhor is a noun phrase, and any noun phrase takes a third person verb
Because the senhor is talking about himself
Because formal Portuguese has no second person
Because senhor is a plural word
exercises.explanation: Senhor means gentleman, so the question literally asks whether the gentleman wants a coffee. Você came from Vossa Mercê and behaves the same way.

exercises.prompt: Which closing is appropriate for a formal email?
exercises.explanation: Atenciosamente is an adverb from atenciosa plus -mente, literally with an attentive mind; Cordialmente is the other standard formal closing.

exercises.prompt: What does the accent on currículo show?
choices: The stress is on the third to last syllable, which the ending does not predict
exercises.explanation: Ending in o predicts the second to last syllable. The stress is on cur-RÍ-cu-lo, one syllable earlier, so a mark is written, and the i takes the acute.

exercises.prompt: Why is residência written with ê and not é?
choices: Every word ending in ia takes a circumflex
The e is a nasal diphthong
The stressed e is followed by n, which nasalizes and closes it
exercises.explanation: The ending ia counts as two syllables, so the stress is third to last and needs a mark. The n nasalizes the e and closes it, so the circumflex is used.

exercises.prompt: How is the acronym CNH said aloud?
exercises.explanation: Acronyms are read by naming the letters. The letter h is silent inside words but its name is agá.

exercises.prompt: Why is it a CNH but o CPF?
choices: Acronyms ending in H are always feminine
Each acronym takes the gender of the noun it abbreviates: carteira is feminine, cadastro is masculine
exercises.explanation: CNH is Carteira Nacional de Habilitação and CPF is Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas. The article agrees with the noun behind the letters.

exercises.prompt: In Venho por meio desta, what is desta?
choices: de + esta, pointing to an omitted feminine noun such as carta
The past tense of a verb
exercises.explanation: The full thought is I come by means of this letter. Esta agrees with the feminine noun it stands for.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal meaning of reconhecer firma?
exercises.explanation: Firma is a signature as a legal mark, not a business; the natural English is to notarize a signature. Firm is a false friend.

exercises.prompt: In seu Henrique, what is seu?
choices: A reduced form of senhor used as a title before a first name
A form of the verb ser
exercises.explanation: It is spelled like the possessive but is a title, like dona before a woman's first name.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly reports a request in everyday speech?
choices: Ela pediu para mim enviar o contrato.
Ela pediu para eu enviei o contrato.
Ela pediu para eu enviar o contrato.
Ela pediu que eu enviar o contrato.
exercises.explanation: The subject of an infinitive is a subject, so it is eu and not mim, and the verb after para is the infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Why is the ss in assinar said [s], while the s in casa is said [z]?
choices: Ss is the way to write [s] between vowels; a single s there is [z]
exercises.explanation: Between vowels, s is [z]. To keep the hiss, Portuguese doubles it: assinar, massa, passo.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a polite refusal?
choices: Infelizmente não será possível neste momento.
exercises.explanation: Infelizmente plus the future tense adds distance; the other three are blunt.

exercises.prompt_pt: Gostaria ___ solicitar uma segunda via do documento.
exercises.hint_en: I would like to request a duplicate of the document.
exercises.explanation: Gostar always takes de, and the de stays before an infinitive.

exercises.prompt_pt: Poderia me ___ onde fica o cartório?
exercises.hint_en: Could you tell me where the notary office is?
exercises.explanation: After poderia, the main verb is in the infinitive. Informar is the more formal choice.

exercises.prompt_pt: Bom dia, ___. O senhor pegou uma senha?
exercises.hint_en: Good morning, sir. Did you take a queue number?
exercises.explanation: When you call someone directly, the article is dropped: senhor, not o senhor. As subject, the article stays: O senhor pegou.

exercises.hint_en: I am writing to request information.
exercises.explanation: De + esta, pointing to the message being written.

exercises.prompt_pt: Ele pediu ___ eu enviar o currículo.
exercises.hint_en: He asked me to send the CV.
exercises.explanation: Pedir para plus the subject plus the infinitive reports a request; the subject stays eu.

exercises.prompt_pt: Preciso só que o senhor ___ aqui.
exercises.hint_en: I just need you to sign here.
exercises.explanation: Precisar que with a different subject needs the subjunctive; assinar changes its final ar to e.

exercises.prompt_pt: Pedimos que a senhora ___ o RG.
exercises.hint_en: We ask that you bring your ID.
exercises.explanation: Pedir que takes the subjunctive; the present main verb gives the present subjunctive of trazer, traga.

exercises.prompt_pt: Infelizmente não ___ possível agendar para hoje.
exercises.hint_en: Unfortunately it will not be possible to schedule for today.
exercises.explanation: The future of ser adds distance; it is the typical formal refusal.
Both are standard closings made with the suffix -mente.

exercises.prompt_en: I would like to schedule an appointment.
answers: Gostaria de agendar um horário.
Eu gostaria de agendar um horário.
Gostaria de marcar um horário.
Eu gostaria de marcar um horário.
Gostaria de agendar um atendimento.
Gostaria de marcar um atendimento.
Gostaria de agendar uma consulta.
Gostaria de marcar uma consulta.

Eu gostaria de marcar um atendimento.
exercises.explanation: Gostaria de plus the infinitive, with de because gostar takes de.

exercises.prompt_en: She asked me to send the contract.
answers: Ela pediu para eu enviar o contrato.
Ela pediu pra eu enviar o contrato.
Ela pediu que eu enviasse o contrato.
Ela me pediu para enviar o contrato.
Ela me pediu pra enviar o contrato.
Ela pediu para eu mandar o contrato.
Ela pediu pra eu mandar o contrato.
exercises.explanation: Pedir para plus eu plus the infinitive, or pedir que plus the imperfect subjunctive.

answers: Segue em anexo o meu currículo.

answers: Infelizmente, não será possível.
